b1.note: More precisely, SharedArrayBuffer construction and shared-memory transfer require a cross-origin-isolated context; the standard deployment is COOP: same-origin plus COEP: require-corp or credentialless, subject to Permissions Policy.

b2.verdict: disagree: Chrome supports timestamp-query, but it is an optional adapter feature rather than something guaranteed to be exposed to every ordinary web page/device by default.
b2.note: Chrome added timestamp-query in 121, but applications must test adapter.features.has('timestamp-query'); current compatibility data marks Chrome/Edge support as partial because exposure depends on platform/adapter.

b3.verdict: disagree: WebAssembly thread/atomic module validation is not the cross-origin-isolation gate; cross-origin isolation gates creation/use of shared WebAssembly memory and the SharedArrayBuffer machinery needed for browser threading.
b3.note: A threads-enabled Wasm binary can validate independently; the browser security restriction is on shared memory/threading use without cross-origin isolation.

rows.claim: SharedArrayBuffer is available to web content when the document is cross-origin isolated; deploy COOP: same-origin together with COEP: require-corp or credentialless, and ensure Permissions Policy does not block cross-origin-isolated.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy; web.dev cross-origin isolation guide
rows.notes: Applies to Chromium-based Chrome and Edge.

rows.claim: SharedArrayBuffer is available when the document is cross-origin isolated using COOP plus COEP; without cross-origin isolation the shared-memory capability is restricted.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Window.crossOriginIsolated and SharedArrayBuffer compatibility
rows.notes: The same web security model applies; verify deployment with window.crossOriginIsolated.

rows.claim: Safari supports SharedArrayBuffer and Wasm threading when the page opts into cross-origin isolation with COOP and COEP; WebKit documents COOP/COEP as the mechanism that re-enables SharedArrayBuffer/Wasm threading.
rows.verifier_hint: WebKit Safari 15.2 COOP/COEP SharedArrayBuffer announcement
rows.notes: Safari's documented deployment requirement is COOP plus COEP.

rows.claim: WebGPU is available for ordinary secure web content and supports compute pipelines/shaders; availability remains platform/adapter dependent.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN WebGPU API; Chrome WebGPU documentation
rows.notes: WebGPU requires a secure context (HTTPS).

rows.claim: WebGPU compute is available in Firefox stable on supported platforms; Windows support is enabled broadly, while macOS support is enabled for Apple Silicon, with other platform coverage still more limited.
rows.verifier_hint: Firefox WebGPU release notes and current experimental-features page
rows.notes: Firefox 141 enabled WebGPU on Windows; Firefox 147 enabled it on Apple Silicon macOS.

rows.claim: WebGPU compute is available in Safari stable; Safari 26 added WebGPU support, subject to the underlying platform/GPU.
rows.verifier_hint: Apple Safari 26 release notes; MDN WebGPU API compatibility
rows.notes: WebGPU is a secure-context API.

rows.claim: No universal guarantee: Chrome/Edge implement timestamp-query, but it is an optional GPUAdapter feature and must be feature-detected; current compatibility data classifies support as partial rather than universal.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN GPUSupportedFeatures timestamp-query; Chrome WebGPU 121 release notes
rows.notes: On supported adapters it is usable from ordinary web content without a special developer flag; do not assume every adapter exposes it.

rows.claim: timestamp-query is not exposed by default in Firefox stable; current compatibility data lists Firefox as unsupported.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN GPUSupportedFeatures feature_timestamp-query; Mozilla WebGPU CTS Bugzilla entries
rows.notes: Firefox has WebGPU itself, but that does not imply support for every optional WebGPU feature.

rows.claim: Safari 26 and later expose timestamp-query in stable Safari; current compatibility data lists Safari 26+ as supported.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use timestamp-query compatibility; Apple Safari 26 release notes
rows.notes: This changed after 2026-03-01 because Safari 26 shipped in 2025.

rows.claim: Supported. WebAssembly threads/atomics are enabled in Chrome and Chromium-based Edge; browser use of shared Wasm memory still requires cross-origin isolation.
rows.verifier_hint: WebAssembly threads feature table; MDN SharedArrayBuffer
rows.notes: Do not confuse Wasm module validation with permission to instantiate/use shared memory.

rows.claim: Supported. Firefox supports WebAssembly threads/atomics; use of shared memory in browser content remains subject to cross-origin isolation.
rows.verifier_hint: WebAssembly threads feature table; MDN crossOriginIsolated
rows.notes: Firefox has supported Wasm threads since Firefox 79.

rows.claim: Supported. Safari supports WebAssembly threads/atomics; SharedArrayBuffer/Wasm threading requires cross-origin isolation.
rows.verifier_hint: WebKit Safari 15.2 release article; current Wasm threads compatibility
rows.notes: Safari's threading support is longstanding.

rows.claim: Supported by default. WebAssembly 128-bit SIMD is supported in Chrome 91+ and Chromium Edge 91+.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use WebAssembly SIMD; Emscripten SIMD documentation
rows.notes: No cross-origin-isolation requirement for ordinary SIMD.

rows.claim: Supported by default. Firefox supports WebAssembly SIMD from Firefox 89 onward.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use WebAssembly SIMD; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: No cross-origin-isolation requirement.

rows.claim: Supported by default. Safari supports WebAssembly SIMD from Safari 16.4 onward.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use WebAssembly SIMD; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: No cross-origin-isolation requirement.

rows.claim: Supported by default. Chrome and Edge support WebAssembly relaxed SIMD from version 114 onward.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN relaxed-SIMD browser-compat data; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: Relaxed SIMD permits hardware-dependent numerical results and should be used only where that is acceptable.

rows.claim: Supported by default in current stable Firefox; Firefox 146 added stable support.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use relaxed-SIMD; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: Firefox 146 shipped December 2025, so this is a post-2026-03-01 support state but not a change during the requested window.

rows.claim: Not supported in stable Safari; current compatibility data lists Safari stable as unsupported, with support only in Safari Technology Preview.
rows.verifier_hint: Can I Use relaxed-SIMD; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: Do not treat Safari Technology Preview support as Safari stable support.

rows.claim: Supported by default in stable Chrome/Edge; Chrome shipped JSPI in version 137 and Edge follows Chromium's implementation.
rows.verifier_hint: Chrome 137 release notes; WebAssembly JSPI browser support
rows.notes: JSPI is a Wasm async-integration facility, not a proving-specific feature.

rows.claim: Supported by default in current stable Firefox 153+; Firefox 153 shipped July 21, 2026.
rows.verifier_hint: Web Platform DX JSPI entry; Mozilla Firefox 153 release information
rows.notes: Current third-party compatibility data records Firefox 153 as the stable default-on release; older WebAssembly feature metadata still shows the earlier flag-gated state and should be treated as stale for this question.

rows.claim: Not supported in stable Safari; current compatibility data lists Safari as unsupported, although Safari Technology Preview has experimental support.
rows.verifier_hint: Web Platform DX JSPI browser support; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: Do not count Safari Technology Preview as Safari stable.

rows.claim: Supported by default. Chrome 133 and Edge 133 added WebAssembly Memory64.
rows.verifier_hint: Web Platform DX Memory64 support; Chrome 133 release notes
rows.notes: Memory64 permits 64-bit memory indexes and memories beyond the 4-GiB 32-bit-addressing ceiling.

rows.claim: Supported by default. Firefox 134 added WebAssembly Memory64.
rows.verifier_hint: Web Platform DX Memory64 support; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: No cross-origin-isolation requirement merely to use Memory64.

rows.claim: Not supported in stable Safari; current browser-support data lists Safari as unsupported.
rows.verifier_hint: Web Platform DX Memory64 support; WebAssembly feature table
rows.notes: Safari Technology Preview support is not listed as stable Safari support.

rows.claim: A cross-origin iframe cannot independently obtain cross-origin isolation merely by setting its own headers. For COI-gated APIs such as SharedArrayBuffer, the embedding top-level context must itself be cross-origin isolated and delegate the cross-origin-isolated capability; WebGPU is separately subject to Permissions Policy and can be delegated with the iframe policy.
rows.verifier_hint: WICG Document Isolation Policy; Chromium cross-origin-isolation iframe tests; W3C Permissions Policy
rows.notes: For WebGPU, distinguish API access from cross-origin isolation: WebGPU does not itself require COI, but an embedding policy can restrict it.

rows.claim: A cross-origin iframe cannot bootstrap COI-gated capabilities independently of its embedding context. The parent must provide the required isolation context and permission delegation; WebGPU access is separately governed by browser support and Permissions Policy.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Permissions Policy; MDN crossOriginIsolated; Mozilla WebGPU status
rows.notes: Firefox's WebGPU availability also remains platform-dependent.

rows.claim: A cross-origin iframe cannot independently bootstrap the COI-gated SharedArrayBuffer environment; the embedding context must satisfy the isolation model and policy delegation. WebGPU itself is separate from COI and is controlled by the browser's WebGPU/Permissions Policy implementation.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Window.crossOriginIsolated; MDN Permissions Policy; WebKit COOP/COEP documentation
rows.notes: Safari supports COOP/COEP SharedArrayBuffer isolation, but embedding constraints still apply.
